basis: snapshot narrativeCache.data (full read). Note: this run is lang=fi analysis output in English narrative fields, spot USD 328.58 vs 339.99 in the single-writer runs — comparable in method, not to the decimal.

justifications.depth: Each pool is a set of one-to-three-sentence headings; Automotive and Energy get four short blocks with no unit economics beyond a margin number. The Autonomy pool is the only one that reasons — and it stops after the required-scale calculation.
justifications.coverage: All four pools present with the reported-segment vs option-segment split stated, but the two cash-generating divisions are covered at fact-sheet level while two thirds of the EV sits in the options.
justifications.logic: The best passage in the series is here: USD 578.5bn of allocated EV needs ~USD 38bn of 2030 EBIT, i.e. USD 95–110bn of revenue, which exceeds the entire conservative 2030 robotaxi market. The report then contradicts itself by pricing the target off a 70.0x multiple, i.e. accepting nearly the same premium it just showed to be unsupported.
justifications.evidence: Dated citations with domains for the milestone claims (RDW approval 10 Apr 2026, Waymo 500k weekly rides, 2.5m paid robotaxi miles). Several economic figures — Optimus USD 50k–100k manufacturing cost, USD 30k ASP, 30% contribution margin — appear without a source.
justifications.valuation: The bridge is a group EV/EBITDA and P/E blend with the SOTP used only as a constraint, so none of the division analysis reaches the target price. The Base scenario lands at USD 328.38 against a USD 328.58 spot, which reads as calibration to the market rather than a derived case.
justifications.readability: Mature production layout, tables populated, no visible contradictions between numbers on the page — the strongest run of the four on presentation.

summary: The multi-stage baseline: production-grade presentation and one genuinely excellent required-scale argument, but the divisions are fact sheets rather than analysis and the target price is derived from a group multiple that ignores everything the report argued. This is the comparison point the single-writer runs beat on depth (2 vs 4) and on bridge consistency, and lose to on presentation (3 vs 2).
issues: Pool deep dives at fact-sheet depth (~2350 words total vs ~7800 in single-writer run 4)
Target multiple 70.0x contradicts the report's own finding that current earnings support ~11% of EV
Base scenario equals spot to within 0.2 USD — reads as market calibration
